frameworks.name: Expectation-Reality Reframing
frameworks.definition: A mental model where life satisfaction is anchored to expectations rather than absolute outcomes; shifting expectations downward increases contentment with the same reality.

frameworks.name: $100 Million Scaling Roadmap
frameworks.definition: A 10-stage framework mapping business growth milestones and identifying common bottlenecks across portfolio companies, with stage-specific priorities for product, marketing, sales, customer success, recruiting, IT, HR, and finance.

claims.text: For most people, life satisfaction depends on the gap between expectations and reality, not the absolute quality of life. Shifting expectations downward closes that gap and increases contentment with identical circumstances.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Contentment is relative to expectation, not absolute outcome; lowering expectation while keeping outcome constant shrinks the gap.

claims.text: Sadness about premature death is not intrinsic to the death itself, but to the violation of an expectation that someone 'should' have lived longer. Reframing the actual duration as lucky rather than short eliminates the sadness.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Sadness stems from unmet expectations ('should'), not from the event; reframing removes the expectation violation.

claims.text: Modern life-expectancy anchors (living to 100) are arbitrary given historical baselines. Average life expectancy 500 years ago was ~35 years; in the Dark Ages it was similar. Most people who achieve 30+ years have already exceeded historical norms.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

numbers.axis: historical life expectancy across time periods

claims.text: At age 36, with average life expectancy of 74, you are mathematically middle-aged by current statistics, though few people emotionally accept this reframing.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Founders who delegate sales (hiring first salesperson before $1M revenue) tend to reach $5M revenue roughly 9 months faster than founders who retained sales personally through $2M+ (Acquisition.com portfolio, 60 businesses, 2019-2022).
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi
claims.mechanism: Delegated sales frees founder to focus on product and positioning rather than daily sales activity, compounding growth velocity.

numbers.axis: time to $5M revenue milestone by sales delegation timing

bounded_by: Does not directly address self-serve SaaS or product-centric businesses where founder sales role differs

claims.text: Alex Hormozi has lived life intentionally and would accept death tomorrow without depression, having 'given it everything' and lived as he intended.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

claims.text: Hanging out with loved ones (family like Layla) more than usual would be the only behavioral change if death were imminent tomorrow; this reflects intentional life design.
claims.speaker: Alex Hormozi

examples.text: Alex Hormozi had a cat he liked that died at 2 years old from a heart condition. Initially he was very sad, reasoning that the cat 'should have lived longer.' But when he reframed the situation—'What if cats only lived 6 months and I got to have him for 2 years?'—he became significantly less sad, shifting from disappointment to gratitude. The same 2-year duration became 'awesome' when expectations were adjusted downward.

Betty White died at 99 and people said she 'lived a good life' without regret. When Kobe Bryant died before his expected lifespan, it was framed as a tragedy. The contrast illustrates that the emotional response to death depends on expectation-vs-reality gap, not the actual event.

practices.text: Shift life-expectancy expectations downward to historical baselines (30-35 years) to increase gratitude for reaching modern ages. Use Jesus's 33-year lifespan as a reference point for significant achievement within a short timeframe.
